topic: Teacher Professional Development: Continuous Professional Development (CPD) and NISHTHA
description: This module covers Continuous Professional Development (CPD) and the NISHTHA program, reflecting NEP 2020's vision to empower and uplift the teaching profession. It highlights the paradigm shift from sporadic, one-time workshops to lifelong learning, mandating annual CPD to equip educators with modern pedagogical skills, inclusive education strategies, and competency-based assessment techniques.

nep_2020_cpd_mandate.concept: NEP 2020 Mandate on Continuous Professional Development (CPD)
key_points: Annual Requirement: NEP 2020 mandates that every teacher and head teacher/principal must participate in at least 50 hours of Continuous Professional Development (CPD) every year.
Self-Driven and Modular: CPD is not meant to be top-down or forced. Teachers are encouraged to self-select modular training programs based on their own professional interests and classroom needs.

Focus Areas: The training focuses heavily on foundational literacy and numeracy (FLN), experiential learning, competency-based education, inclusive education, and the use of technology/AI in education.

nishtha_program.concept: NISHTHA (National Initiative for School Heads' and Teachers' Holistic Advancement)
key_points: What it is: NISHTHA is the world’s largest integrated teacher training program launched by the Ministry of Education. Its goal is to build the capacities of teachers and school principals at the elementary and secondary stages.

Digital Transition: Originally designed as a face-to-face cascade training model, it successfully transitioned to a 100% online, self-paced format delivered via the DIKSHA portal during and after the COVID-19 pandemic.

Holistic Advancement: Unlike traditional training that only focused on subject-matter expertise, NISHTHA trains teachers on 'how to teach' (pedagogy), focusing on socio-emotional learning, mental health (Manodarpan), and creating joyful, stress-free classrooms.

npst_and_career_progression.concept: National Professional Standards for Teachers (NPST) and Career Progression
key_points: Defining Standards: NEP 2020 tasks the NCTE (National Council for Teacher Education) with developing the NPST. These standards clearly define what constitutes 'good teaching' at different levels of expertise (e.g., Beginner, Proficient, Expert, Lead Teacher).

Merit-Based Promotion: Historically, teacher promotions were often based strictly on seniority (years of service). NEP 2020 shifts this to a merit-based system, where career progression is directly tied to the accumulation of CPD hours, peer reviews, and demonstrated teaching effectiveness.

questions.question: According to the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, how many hours of Continuous Professional Development (CPD) must every teacher and head teacher participate in annually?
questions.explanation: NEP 2020 mandates a minimum of 50 hours of CPD annually for all teachers and school heads to ensure they continuously upskill and stay updated with the latest pedagogical practices.

questions.question: A middle school teacher wants to complete her mandatory CPD hours by taking courses on 'Integrating Toy-Based Pedagogy' and 'Managing Classroom Mental Health'. Which national platform/initiative is specifically designed to provide these holistic, integrated capacity-building modules?
questions.explanation: NISHTHA (National Initiative for School Heads' and Teachers' Holistic Advancement) is the flagship integrated teacher training program hosted on the DIKSHA portal, offering diverse modules on pedagogy, mental health, and inclusive education.

mcq_bank.subtopic: NPST and the Paradigm Shift in Teaching

questions.question: Why does NEP 2020 mandate the creation of the National Professional Standards for Teachers (NPST) and tie career progression to CPD rather than just seniority?

options.A: To create a bureaucratic hurdle to prevent teachers from getting regular salary increments.
options.B: To shift the teaching profession from a stagnant, seniority-based system to a dynamic, merit-based system that rewards continuous learning, pedagogical innovation, and actual classroom effectiveness.
options.C: Because older teachers are deemed incapable of using modern technology.
options.D: To force all existing teachers to eventually resign and make way for private educators.

questions.explanation: The core objective of NPST and the CPD mandate is to professionalize teaching. By linking promotions to merit, continuous upskilling (CPD), and proven classroom impact, the policy aims to motivate teachers to actively improve their pedagogical skills throughout their careers.
